title: Locked design: every rule written and committed before any return of these baskets was computed
provenance: The plan was committed before the returns engine first ran. Sections 0-9 of the plan are unchanged since the lock; two dated addenda follow it. These are repository timestamps, not an independent external timestamp attestation.
seen_before_lock: No forward return of these baskets, or of the S&P 500 fund over their windows, was computed, printed or read before the lock. One exception, in another universe: an earlier topic-shortlist probe printed one-year returns of 60 large US listings and of the S&P 500 fund over those windows; none is a basket window. Scripts before it read only reference data, which tickers traded on a date, trailing dollar volume and, to link a renamed ticker, the closes around one hand-off day.
blind_review: An independent blind review read the draft plan and every lab script before the lock and computed no return: 14 findings (3 blocker, 5 major, 6 minor), each fixed or answered before the lock.
question: At a public hype moment, does buying every listed company in the hot stock's industry, the hot stock itself left out, beat the S&P 500 over three years, as a basket and as its typical stock?

A1.basket: chip makers: semiconductors, solar-cell makers included

A2.event: Tesla's first session in the S&P 500

A3.basket: medicinal and botanical products: 3 cannabis growers, 5 supplement makers, 2 drug developers

A4.event: Pfizer and BioNTech announce their vaccine's interim efficacy result
A4.basket: biotech (biologics); two vaccine makers among them

A5.event: first session after Zoom's blowout quarter

A7.event: OpenAI releases ChatGPT: the software half of the same day

S1.event: first session after Nvidia's May 2023 earnings report
S1.basket: chip makers: semiconductors, solar-cell makers included

S2.event: the Tesla moment dated at year-end 2020 instead

B-XOM.event: first day in our data (from 2004) that Exxon Mobil was America's most-traded stock

B-JPM.event: first day in our data (from 2004) that JPMorgan Chase was America's most-traded stock

B-AMZN.event: first day in our data (from 2004) that Amazon was America's most-traded stock

B-NVDA.event: first day in our data (from 2004) that Nvidia was America's most-traded stock
B-NVDA.basket: semiconductors (Enphase, a solar company, files under this code)

B-TSLA.event: first day in our data (from 2004) that Tesla was America's most-traded stock

rule_picked_events.reason: the hot stock has no readable industry code on the date
the same industry code as a kept event less than three years earlier
the same industry code as a kept event less than three years earlier

rule_picked_rule: On every session, rank common stocks and ADRs by trailing 20-session mean dollar volume. An event is the first session a stock is number one for the first time in our data (from 2004); the basket is every other identified company with its industry code that day. Dropped: an unidentified leader, a catch-all code, a code kept under three years earlier, fewer than 10 members.
membership: Every ticker with a daily bar on the date whose reference row is common stock or an ADR with an SEC registrant number; one row per registrant. Identity is tested against the company's own SEC filings; reused tickers are linked to a successor or bounded as unidentified. The industry code is the one in the company's own SEC filing header as of the date.
returns: Buy at the close on the moment date; hold one and three years. Total return with dividends reinvested on the ex-date (split-scaled). A listing that ends is followed to the same registrant or a matched successor (at most 3 hand-offs), else sold at its last close with the cash at 0%. Equal weight at entry, no rebalancing. The S&P 500 = the SPY fund by the same method.
data_check: Any member-day above +300% or below -75% is flagged and listed; flagged members stay in the registered result and are removed in a fragility variant.
metrics: whole basket vs the S&P 500, in points
typical stock (the median member) vs the S&P 500
members beating the S&P 500, N of M
listings that ended: collapsed (exited at a fifth or less of the entry price) or ended otherwise
the basket without its best member and without its best five
after the run: the hot stock had already more than doubled in the 252 sessions before the moment

verdict_rule.K1: the whole basket beat the S&P 500 over 3 years (gap above zero)
verdict_rule.K2: the typical stock beat it over 3 years
verdict_rule.robust: the rule-picked moments read the same label and every leave-one-out label agrees; otherwise the label is called FRAGILE
fragility_families: unidentified companies at -100% and at the 90th percentile

limits: Moment choice is partly ours; the rule-picked moments are the guard.
Unidentified companies and last-close exits flatter the baskets; cash at 0% and missed spin-offs cut the other way.
The moments overlap; this is a count, not a significance test.
The S&P 500 over these windows includes strong bull runs.

addenda.change: A serialization fix after the first run printed every result; the rerun printed 14 of 14 moment lines identical. No computation changed.
A factual correction of descriptive prose: the cannabis basket is 3 cannabis growers, 5 supplement makers and 2 drug developers (not 7 supplement makers). No rule or number changed.
